title: The Lost key in the snow
subtitle: 安全预防 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：安全预防（人与自然·灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：lost　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lost 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the elder wrote of ① a lost key in the snow in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② so lost that nobody in the village would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the lost ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the lost key in the snow that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1944 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too lost to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the lost ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a lost child at the station, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as lost as the child at the station they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was lost or not, and he said so.

By 1957 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something lost, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite lost; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the lost ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1960, twice over, she wrote of another lost key in the snow in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less lost than anybody had expected. ⑩ The lost child at the station that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1962, was the one she could never quite name; the lost ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 丢失（前置定语 a lost key in the snow：1950 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件丢失的钥匙）
B. adj. 丢失／迷路（两处加强说法：so lost that … 与 no less lost than …）
C. adj. 丢失／迷路（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 丢失（表语 too lost to do：母亲觉得它太丢失，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 迷路（前置定语 a lost child at the station：叔叔把整件事称作一桩迷路的孩子）
F. adj. 迷路（同级比较 as lost as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩车站里迷路的孩子相比）
G. adj. 迷路（后置定语 something lost：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 迷路（受程度副词修饰 quite lost：那位后生的评价）

items.q: a lost key in the snow
the lost key in the snow that
a lost child at the station
The lost child at the station that

answers.why: lost 意为“丢失”，1950 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件丢失的钥匙”，此处作前置定语 a lost key in the snow。
lost 意为“丢失”，此处用 so lost that 结构，说它丢失到村子里没人敢靠近。
lost 意为“丢失”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的丢失雪地里丢失的钥匙，等于最高级的说法。
lost 意为“丢失”，母亲认为这件东西“太丢失了，谁也用不上”，too lost to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
lost 意为“迷路”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩迷路的孩子”，此处作前置定语 a lost child at the station。
lost 意为“迷路”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩车站里迷路的孩子一样迷路”，同级比较用 as lost as。
lost 意为“迷路”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“迷路的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something lost。
lost 意为“迷路”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当迷路”，quite 修饰原级 lost。
lost 意为“迷路”，no less lost than 表示“其迷路不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之迷路不亚于任何人的预料。
lost 意为“迷路”，母亲 1962 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的迷路孩子”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1950 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件丢失的钥匙。（a lost key in the snow）
它丢失到村子里没有一个人敢靠近。（so lost that …）
母亲觉得它太丢失，谁也用不上。（too lost to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩迷路的孩子。（a lost child at the station）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩车站里迷路的孩子一样迷路。（as lost as …）
到了 1957 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件迷路的东西。（something lost）
answers: In 1950 the elder wrote of a lost key in the snow in the memoir.
It was so lost that nobody in the village would go near it.
My mother thought it too lost to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a lost child at the station.
He said nobody would call it as lost as the child at the station they had once had.
By 1957 the memoir asked for nothing but something lost.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 lost 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the elder wrote of a lost key in the snow in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the lost key in the snow that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too lost to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a lost child at the station, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite lost, and everybody laughed.
The lost ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
